Baire Class 1 Functions

Pointwise limits of continuous functions — Baire class 1. Thomae's function T(p/q)=1/qT(p/q) = 1/qT(p/q)=1/q (reduced), T(x)=0T(x) = 0T(x)=0 (irrational) is the pointwise limit of sums fnf_nfn​ of disjoint tents. TTT is continuous at irrationals, discontinuous at rationals — a living example of Baire's theorem that the continuity points contain a dense GδG_\deltaGδ​.

Show proof
  1. First, why the sum is over reduced fractions only. Summing over all pairs (p,q)(p, q)(p,q) counts each rational many times (1/2=2/4=3/6=⋯1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 = \cdots1/2=2/4=3/6=⋯): at x=1/2x = 1/2x=1/2 the stacked heights 1/2+1/4+1/6+⋯1/2 + 1/4 + 1/6 + \cdots1/2+1/4+1/6+⋯ would diverge, so the sum could never converge to Thomae. With reduced fractions each rational appears exactly once.
  2. Each tent x↦tri(n3(x−p/q))x \mapsto \mathrm{tri}(n^3(x - p/q))x↦tri(n3(x−p/q)) is continuous (a composition of continuous maps), and the sum is finite (at most ∑q≤n(q+1)\sum_{q \le n}(q+1)∑q≤n​(q+1) terms), so fnf_nfn​ is continuous. Also fn≥0f_n \ge 0fn​≥0.
  3. The tents are pairwise disjoint. Hence the spacing is always ≥1/(n(n−1))\ge 1/(n(n-1))≥1/(n(n−1)).

The rationals with 1/b≥ε1/b \ge \varepsilon1/b≥ε, i.e. denominator b≤Mb \le Mb≤M, are finitely many in [x0−1,x0+1][x_0 - 1, x_0 + 1][x0​−1,x0​+1]. Let δ\deltaδ be the minimum distance from x0x_0x0​ to this finite set (δ>0\delta > 0δ>0 since x0x_0x0​ is irrational). Then for ∣x−x0∣<δ|x - x_0| < \delta∣x−x0​∣<δ: if xxx is rational its denominator exceeds MMM, so T(x)<εT(x) < \varepsilonT(x)<ε; if irrational, T(x)=0T(x) = 0T(x)=0. Thus ∣T(x)−T(x0)∣<ε|T(x) - T(x_0)| < \varepsilon∣T(x)−T(x0​)∣<ε — TTT is continuous at x0x_0x0​.
  3. Hence the continuity set is exactly the irrationals R∖Q\mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Q}R∖Q. Each singleton {p/q}\{p/q\}{p/q} is closed, so its complement is open, and R∖Q=⋂q≥1⋃p(R∖{p/q})\mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Q} = \bigcap_{q \ge 1}\bigcup_{p}(\mathbb{R} \setminus \{p/q\})R∖Q=⋂q≥1​⋃p​(R∖{p/q}) is a countable intersection of open sets — a GδG_\deltaGδ​. The irrationals are dense, so it is a dense GδG_\deltaGδ​.
